title: Subscriber stepdown and evidence checklist — customer-facing draft
content:
Purpose
This is a customer-facing (but editable) status+guidance draft for a subscriber-visible stepdown event that caused degraded responses for a subset of tenants. The doc is intended to be used as an update on status.redwood.ai and as an attached evidence/checklist for customers who request verification or replay access.

TL;DR (for status page)
We observed a sequenced stepdown in one of our inference pools that led to slow or truncated responses for some tenant requests between 2026-07-14T22:12:00Z and 2026-07-14T23:04:00Z. Mitigations were applied and normal service resumed by 2026-07-14T23:15:00Z. No customer data was lost or altered. Options: (1) automatic rollback/replay for eligible requests (opt-in), (2) replay kit for customers to validate outputs, (3) acceptance of processed outputs as-is. This doc explains those choices, what we verified, and next steps.

Audience and framing
Primary audience: engineering & ops contacts at affected customers + platform/product managers who may need to coordinate replays or audits. Secondary audience: security/compliance reviewers who want evidence of data integrity. This is intentionally pragmatic — includes concrete verification steps and a short timeline.

Scope & impact summary
- Affected tenants: ~47 tenants routed through pool-west-3 (subset flagged by our routing heuristics).
- Symptoms: intermittent slow responses (>3s per token) and truncated multi-turn responses (stream cut early) for requests with long context (>2,048 tokens).
- User-visible client impact: increased latency and in ~2% of requests truncated output or early streaming termination. No successful requests returned incorrect content beyond truncation.
- Data integrity: request payloads logged only for debugging (redacted) and were not modified. There is no evidence of data corruption or unauthorized access.

High-level timeline (UTC)
- 2026-07-14T22:11:45 — anomaly detection alerted: increased prefix-cache eviction for pool-west-3.
- 2026-07-14T22:12:00 — automated circuit-breaker attempted graceful stepdown to fallback model variant. Some in-flight requests experienced stream termination.
- 2026-07-14T22:18:30 — SRE began targeted routing changes to move tenant traffic to pool-west-1 fallback.
- 2026-07-14T22:45:00 — partial recovery observed; however a configuration race caused two short re-evictions at 22:51 and 23:02.
- 2026-07-14T23:04:00 — the final mitigation (stateful KV-cache pinning + reduced batch window) was applied.
- 2026-07-14T23:15:00 — system returned to normal latency and streaming stability.

Root cause (short)
An aggressive automated stepdown policy triggered when cache pressure exceeded a heuristic threshold for pool-west-3. During the stepdown, a race between the routing controller and the cache-rebuilder caused multiple rapid cache eviction cycles for a narrow window of tenants. This led to failed/aborted streaming for some in-flight long-context sessions. Engineering has reproduced the race in a staging environment and confirmed the controller logic that allowed overlapping rebuilds.

What we verified internally
- Verified there were no successful unauthorized modifications to request/response bodies; all persisted records match incoming request checksums.
- Confirmed affected requests were either service errors (stream termination) or higher-latency but returned contents otherwise intact when completed.
- Cross-checked metrics: token accounting and billing metrics were adjusted to exclude aborted tokens in the affected window (customers will not be charged for aborted token emission).

Customer options (choose one)
1) Opt-in automatic replay (recommended for customers with strict correctness requirements)
   - What it does: We replay eligible requests that were truncated or returned with errors during the incident window using the model variant that was active at request time. Replays will be executed with an isolation policy (no cross-tenant caching) to match original conditions as closely as possible.
   - Eligibility: requests that were recorded as truncated/terminated and that include customer consent for replay. We will provide a list of request IDs for approval.
   - Timeline: replays queued within 48 hours after consent; bulk replays completed within 5 business days depending on volume.

2) Evidence kit + replay guide (self-serve verification)
   - What we provide: (a) a short CSV of request IDs, timestamps, and outcome flags; (b) a signed hash bundle that proves stored request checksums; (c) a step-by-step replay guide for tenant engineers to re-run the requests against the verified model endpoint in a sandbox account.
   - When to choose: customers who prefer to run verification themselves or who need to perform compliance checks.

3) No action / accept outputs as delivered
   - What it means: no replays; accept existing outcomes. Useful for teams where partial truncation does not materially affect product behavior.

How to request a choice (process)
- Reply to this status update or open a ticket with "Incident RI-4218 replay request" in the subject.
- Required fields: contact person, preferred option (1/2/3), list of tenant IDs to include, and whether you require signed evidence of checksums.
- Deadline for bulk automatic replay opt-in: 2026-07-22 23:59:00 UTC (reason: we retain warm caches and deterministic state for a short window; after this date replay fidelity for certain long-context requests may degrade).

What we need from customers for replays
- Consent to re-execute requests (explicit opt-in).
- If your requests include uploaded user data sensitive under your policy, please indicate consent for reprocessing that data for the replay. We will provide a processed-only option where PII is masked if requested.

Evidence checklist included in the attachment
- CSV list of affected request IDs + truncated flag (sample provided)
- Signed hash manifest for request payloads (SHA256 list)
- Short SRE verification log excerpt showing cache eviction events (timestamps + pool id)
- Model variant mapping for pool-west-3 during 22:00–23:30 UTC
- Billing adjustment statement (tokens excluded from billing for aborted emits)

Customer-facing note about billing
We will exclude aborted-token charges from customer billing for the affected window. Customers enrolled in committed-capacity/Dedicated contracts will see an off-cycle credit applied; self-serve/hosted customers will see a billing adjustment reflected on their next invoice with a transparent line-item referencing RI-4218.

Security & compliance
No evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized access. All logs shared in the evidence kit are redacted or pseudonymized by default. If you require full unredacted logs for audit, we will coordinate under an NDA and support ticket — provide contact in the replay request.

Draft messaging for status.redwood.ai (short)
Title: Partial streaming termination in pool-west-3 — rolling recovery
Summary: We experienced a transient stepdown in a single inference pool that caused intermittent streaming termination for a subset of tenants. Mitigations applied; service restored. Customers may opt-in to replays or request an evidence kit. Link to full customer advisory.

Draft email template (concise)
Subject: Action available: replay & evidence for incident RI-4218 (pool-west-3)
Body: Hello — we resolved a transient stepdown that impacted streaming for some requests on 2026-07-14. No data loss. We are offering replay and evidence options; reply to this message with your choice or open a ticket. If you want the full evidence kit or to opt-in to automatic replay, include the tenant IDs and a contact. SRE contact: sresupport@redwood.ai.

Internal notes / TODOs before publishing
- Get SRE + Security sign-off on the hash manifest and redaction approach. (owner: Ethan Park)
- Confirm final list of affected tenant IDs with routing team (owner: Sofia Ruiz).
- Legal review of replay consent language for customers in regulated geos (owner: Noah Reed).
- Prepare billing adjustment memo for finance to apply credits (owner: Maya Gonzalez).

Open questions (for leadership/ops)
- Should we widen the replay deadline to 14 days for a small set of eligible Dedicated tenants that require longer approval windows? (pros/cons: fidelity vs. scheduling complexity)
- Do we offer a reduced-priority replay SLA for high-volume customers to avoid queue starvation for other active workloads?

Contact & next steps
Primary contact: Maya Gonzalez (customer-success) — maya.gonzalez@redwood.ai
SRE lead: Ethan Park — ethan.park@redwood.ai
Legal (replay consent): Noah Reed — noah.reed@redwood.ai

Draft version history
- 2026-07-15 v0.1 initial draft
- 2026-07-17 v0.2 added evidence checklist and billing language
- 2026-07-20 v0.3 updated timeline and sign-off owners (current)

Notes to CS rep using this doc
- Prefer short, plain-language headers when publishing to status page.
- Attach only the redacted evidence bundle by default; escalate unredacted requests through security.
- Track opt-ins in ticket RI-4218 with labels: replay-request / evidence-provided / billing-credit-requested.
